column1: # Golden verdict table. Columns: path, expect_exit, expect_mode, expect_rule_prefix
# $FIX expands to the fixture root, $HOME to the home directory.
# Asserted in tests/test_denylist.sh instead: ~/Library/Mobile Documents does
# not exist on a Mac that has never been signed into iCloud, and guard_path
# returns E_ENOENT before any rule is consulted.
# A symlink is unlinked as itself, never followed, so one pointing at /System
# is refused by default-deny rather than by escape detection. Either way: denied.
# parent /usr is restricted, so this holds on any Mac. The previous row used
# /usr/local/bin, which only exists once something creates it -- on the
# author's machine, macFUSE -- and returned E_ENOENT elsewhere. Same bug as
# $TMPDIR resolves under /private/var/folders, which is an explicit deny. That
# the fixture itself is refused is the correct outcome, and it is why reclaim
# tests must override CMAI_DENYLIST rather than relying on a temp directory.
# ---- a real path covered by no rule at all: default-deny must fire ----
# $PROBE is created by test_guard.sh under /tmp. It has to be somewhere no rule
# covers AND whose parent carries no sunlnk flag: /Users and /Applications both
# do, so a child of either would exercise the parent-flag check instead. It also
# has to be a path that exists on any machine, which is why the test creates it
# rather than assuming a directory such as $HOME/Development is present.
# Rule precedence is asserted in tests/test_denylist.sh instead, which drives
# the rule table directly and so needs no files inside protected directories.
